headline: Market research firm Counterpoint forecasts that the world's humanoid robots will need more than 20 times as much DRAM memory in total in 2030 as this year.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a research-firm forecast with a clear link to the memory-chip industry, but a forecast to 2030 relayed second-hand.
importance_line: It suggests humanoid robots could become a new customer for memory-chip makers such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, after AI data centres, but it is a forecast for 2030 that depends on how many robots are actually built and sold.
summary: Chosunbiz reports that Counterpoint Research expects demand for DRAM, the fast working memory used in computing devices, from humanoid robots to rise more than 20-fold, from about 8,300 terabits this year to about 172,000 terabits in 2030, because more robots will be in use and the average memory per robot is expected to more than double from 19 to 39 gigabytes. Chosunbiz says this would open a new market for memory makers such as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, but the figures are a research firm's projection, not a result.
notes: Read from the pre-fetched full text (the link was cleaned of the amp output parameter; it opens). Counterpoint's own note was not read; the forecast is relayed by Chosunbiz.
